subject: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Emily — really appreciate the context on your search-and-summarization use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Goal: Improve customer support search relevance and shorten time-to-answer for agents while keeping PII out of training/analytics.
2) Recommended pilot scope: 50k weekly queries routed to a dedicated endpoint for 6 weeks, monitor latency and quality via the Redwood Console.
3) Model recommendations (high level): See Rishi's note below for model/quantization suggestions and the benchmark link.

Immediate asks for you (so we can create an eval and build prompt sets):
- Share 30–50 representative customer prompts (anonymized). Examples: typical queries, long transcripts, and edge-case inputs that should be redacted.
- Indicate any data categories that must be redacted or tokenized before hitting the model (PII, credit card, SSN, PHI).

I've attached a quick prompt_set_template.csv you can use — it's intentionally simple (prompt, expected_behavior, redact_flag). If it helps, you can drop a Drive link or reply with the file.

Next steps from us: Rishi will run a light benchmark against the candidate models and send a short recommendation + sample eval metrics. We'll then align on redaction guidance and a mutual action plan.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

Attachments: prompt_set_template.csv (CSV stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Hi team — following up from today's call with a short model fit note and links to the quick benchmark I ran using Acme-like sample traffic. High level:

- Candidate models: gpt-neo-3.7b-8k (good latency/cost), redwood-turbo-11b-q4 (best quality/latency balance for longer context), and redwood-claude-xxl (higher quality, higher cost).
- Quantization: For cost-sensitive pilots we recommend q4_0 for the 11b variant; q8_0 for the 3.7b when latency is critical.
- Benchmarks (small synthetic set): 95th pct latency: 120 ms (3.7b q8), 250 ms (11b q4), 420 ms (xxl). Quality (topline F1 on intent extraction): 0.78 / 0.87 / 0.91 respectively. Full results: https://redwood-benchmarks.s3.amazonaws.com/acme/2026-03-19-results.pdf

Prompt engineering notes: For search + summarization we recommend a two-step prompt set: (1) query normalization + intent extraction, (2) targeted retrieval + concise summarization. The prompt_set_template.csv Marissa attached maps nicely to that flow.

Redaction guidance for the prompt sets: please flag any examples with PII in the 'redact_flag' column. If you need, we can provide a small redaction lambda to run client-side before upload (see Drive link).

Action items:
- Emily: drop the 30–50 anonymized prompts into the template (or share a Drive link).
- Marissa/Rishi: we'll ingest and run a 1k-sample eval, then share a short report and recommended pilot config.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up to walk through the benchmark.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8421 | Prompt collection folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmePromptCollection

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Thanks, Marissa and Rishi — appreciate the thorough notes and the benchmark. Attaching a first pass of 35 prompts (acme_initial_prompts.txt) — these are redacted but we included a few examples marked "POTENTIAL_PII" where we weren't sure about redaction rules.

Questions from our side:
- For prompts with potential PII, do you recommend removing sensitive tokens entirely or replacing them with placeholders (e.g., <NAME>, <ACCOUNT_ID>)?
- Will the redaction lambda run locally in our VPC, or do you ingest raw prompts for the eval? We prefer local redaction and then sharing sanitized prompts.

FWIW, we're leaning toward the 11b q4 option based on your notes — good balance of latency and quality for our use case.

Emily Carter
Director, Search & Discovery, Acme Corporation
emily.carter@acme.com

Attachments: acme_initial_prompts.txt (text stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Great — thanks for the file, Emily. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Redaction: Replace sensitive tokens with placeholders (preferred) rather than removing entirely. Placeholders keep intent/context (e.g., <NAME>, <EMAIL>, <ORDER_ID>). Please mark the original category in the redact_flag column so our eval metrics can bucket results.
2) Redaction lambda: we will provide a small client-side script that runs in your environment (you can run it in the VPC); we do not need raw PII from you. Rishi, I'll loop you in to share the script and a short README in the Drive folder.
3) Pilot config: we'll prepare a 1k-sample eval on redwood-turbo-11b-q4 and gpt-neo-3.7b-q8 to show cost/quality tradeoffs. Aim to have the eval report back to you by next Wednesday (2026-03-25).

Can you confirm: (a) you'll upload the sanitized prompts to the shared Drive folder above, and (b) any additional edge cases we should prioritize (long transcripts, foreign-language queries, intentionally noisy text)?

I'll follow up with the redaction script and a lightweight ingestion checklist. Thanks again — excited to get this running.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

Related: HubSpot deal RDW-DEAL-8421 | Benchmark PDF: https://redwood-benchmarks.s3.amazonaws.com/acme/2026-03-19-results.pdf
